text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Employment and Solidarity Minister Martine Aubry calls for a 35-hour working week and a boost in consumer spending to help employment.

-- Eurotunnel chairman Patrick Ponsolle in an interview calls on shareholders to vote in favour of the financial restructuring to be presented to shareholders on July 10, warns the Channel Tunnel operator might be forece to declare bankruptcy if shareholders reject the plan.
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux subsidiary Sita buys Waste Management France for 650 million francs.
-- Canal Plus subscriber TV channel to pull out of German channel Premiere.
-- Credit Lyonnais expects a 2 billion francs profit for 1997, after implementing a cost-cutting programme, despite rising estimates of its total losses.
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for a summit on water-related issues in Paris next year.
-- U.S. investment fund Templeton holds a five percent stake in BNP bank, becomes the bank's second largest shareholder after Axa -UAP.
-- Commercial court blocks sale to state holding EPFR of a 24.6 percent stake in Artemis holding by CDR company selling off Credit Lyonnais assets.

-- According to 1996 estimates by unemployment fund Unedic, systematic retirement after forty years in activity, called for by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, would cost between 26.4 and 39.5 billion francs through the year 2000.
-- French bourse association and Germany's Deutsche Borse resume talks to create alliances between the French and German financial markets.
-- Air France needs more pilots to operate satisfactorily, recent strike on pilots' contracts and wages hampers hiring of new pilots.
